acceptance_criteria: The governed AID client is exercised end to end using the configured provider route.
The run demonstrates that request submission, provider invocation, response handling, and governed result validation complete successfully.
Evidence identifies the provider route used for the validation run.
risks: Provider credentials, network availability, or provider-side limits may prevent completion.
Provider routing configuration may differ between local and governed environments.
tasks.title: Execute governed AID client end-to-end validation

acceptance_criteria: All applicable local gates are run and their outcomes are recorded.
The validation confirms local gate selection and execution remain explicit and traceable.
Any skipped or unavailable gate has a documented reason and impact.
risks: Unavailable tooling or environment prerequisites can leave a local gate unexecuted.
Gate results may be non-deterministic if dependent services or fixtures are unstable.
tasks.title: Verify local gate execution traceability

acceptance_criteria: The implementation plan records the end-to-end validation result, local gate outcomes, and provider routing evidence.
The plan preserves explicit links between validation activities, dependencies, risks, and acceptance criteria.
The final record is sufficient for an independent reviewer to trace governed delivery decisions.
risks: Incomplete evidence capture can make routing or gate decisions unverifiable.
Subsequent configuration changes may invalidate recorded provider-routing evidence.
tasks.title: Document governed validation evidence
